cards.front: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients with fewer than 4 cycles a year need induced [___] (with combined oral contraceptive pill or cyclic progestogen) to prevent endometrial hyperplasia.
cards.context:
In PCOS the persistent anovulation means unopposed oestrogen drives continuous endometrial proliferation without the cyclic progesterone-driven shedding that protects the lining in normal cycles.

The fix is to recreate the missing progesterone signal. COCP delivers cyclic progestogen plus contraception (ideal in young women planning pregnancy later).

cards.front: Trisomy 21 is the most common viable aneuploidy because the chromosome involved is the smallest [___]. Risk rises with maternal age.
cards.context:
Maternal age drives aneuploidy risk — oocyte meiotic spindle errors accumulate (non-disjunction during meiosis I dominates).

T21 (Down) is the commonest viable trisomy — chromosome 21 is the smallest autosome (fewer genes, less developmental disruption); T13 (Patau) + T18 (Edwards) usually lethal in infancy.

cards.front: Suspected chorioamnionitis: give broad-spectrum antibiotics and plan [___] — do not prolong pregnancy.
cards.context:
Chorioamnionitis (intra-amniotic infection) is bacterial colonisation of fetal membranes, amniotic fluid, and placenta — typically ascending after ROM.

Delivery is part of source control — leaving an infected uterus prolongs sepsis and worsens neonatal outcomes.

Empirical IV antibiotics (amoxicillin/clindamycin + gentamicin, or piperacillin-tazobactam) + delivery; vaginal if labour progressing, CS if obstetric indication.

cards.front: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk is ~10× higher in pregnancy and even higher postpartum, peaking in the first [___] weeks after delivery (Virchow's triad).
cards.context:
VTE risk in pregnancy is ~5-10× non-pregnant baseline; in the first 6 weeks postpartum it's 20-80× higher, peaking weeks 1-2 after delivery.

Virchow's triad fires on all three cylinders postpartum: endothelial damage from delivery, stasis from immobility (worse after CS or epidural-related delayed mobilisation), persistent hypercoagulable state.

VTE remains a leading direct cause of maternal mortality in Australia, mostly preventable with prophylaxis.

cards.front: Trisomy [___] is the most common viable aneuploidy because the chromosome involved is the smallest autosome. Risk rises with maternal age.
cards.context:
Maternal age drives aneuploidy risk — oocyte meiotic spindle errors accumulate (non-disjunction during meiosis I dominates).

T21 (Down) is the commonest viable trisomy — chromosome 21 is the smallest autosome (fewer genes, less developmental disruption); T13 (Patau) + T18 (Edwards) usually lethal in infancy.

cards.front: Neonatal hypoglycaemia: BGL <2.6 mmol/L; at-risk groups (LGA, IDM, SGA, preterm) need BGL check at [___] hours; symptomatic → IV dextrose 10%.
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia (BGL <2.6 mmol/L) is the commonest metabolic problem in newborns.

Screen at-risk infants: BGL at 1-2 h then before feeds for ≥12-24 h.

cards.front: Normal pregnancy arterial blood gas (ABG) shows a chronic compensated [___] alkalosis with PaCO₂ around 30 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ around 18-22 mmol/L.
cards.context: The driver is progesterone, which acts on the central respiratory chemoreceptors to raise tidal volume by ~40% (rate is unchanged). The kidneys then excrete bicarbonate to keep pH near the upper limit of normal.

cards.front: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is [___] causing RUQ pain — a complication of PID (ascending genital-tract infection); classic finding is 'violin-string' adhesions at laparoscopy.
cards.context:
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis is perihepatitis from pelvic infection (classically chlamydia or gonorrhoea) tracking up the right paracolic gutter.

Laparoscopy is pathognomonic: 'violin-string' adhesions between liver capsule and anterior abdominal wall. Treat the underlying pelvic inflammatory disease (ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole).

cards.front: Pelvic organ prolapse management is guided by [___] rather than stage — many women are asymptomatic and require no treatment. Pessaries are a non-surgical option at any stage.
cards.context:
Prolapse is graded with POP-Q, but the grade correlates poorly with how a woman actually feels — a stage 2 cystocele can be very symptomatic while a stage 3 may cause little bother.

Because the goal is relief of symptoms, not a normal anatomical score, an asymptomatic prolapse needs no treatment regardless of grade. Operating on anatomy alone risks complications for no functional gain.

cards.front: Normal cardiotocograph (CTG): baseline 110-160 bpm, variability [___] bpm, accelerations present, no decelerations.
cards.context:
Normal CTG has four reassuring features: baseline 110-160 bpm (bradycardia <110 may be cord/heart block, tachycardia >160 may be sepsis/hypoxia).

DR C BRAVADO structures interpretation: Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline Rate, Variability, Accelerations, Decelerations, Overall.

cards.front: The first-line treatment for significant neonatal unconjugated jaundice is [___].
cards.context: Phototherapy converts unconjugated bilirubin in the skin to water-soluble isomers the baby can excrete. It's plotted against age-specific thresholds; exchange transfusion is reserved for dangerously high levels.

cards.front: Haemodilution in pregnancy is protective: the drop in blood [___] improves uteroplacental blood flow and cushions the red-cell loss of haemorrhage at delivery.
cards.context: Explains why a 'lower' haemoglobin here is adaptive, not pathological — the expanded, less viscous plasma optimises placental perfusion.

cards.front: Neonatal seizures present subtly (lip-smacking, eye deviation, cycling limb movements, apnoea) rather than as classic tonic-clonic activity. The most common cause is HIE (~60%), treated with therapeutic [___] within 6 h.
cards.context:
Neonatal seizures present differently from older children's because the immature brain has limited capacity for generalised tonic-clonic activity.

HIE accounts for ~60% and is treatable with therapeutic hypothermia within 6 h — every minute matters.

Workup: BGL (hypoglycaemia → 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg) and electrolytes (Ca, Mg, Na) — all reversible causes. First-line phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg IV loading; pyridoxine trial for refractory.

cards.front: Empirical antibiotics for early-onset neonatal sepsis: benzylpenicillin (covers GBS) + [___] (covers Gram-negatives like E. coli); stop at 36-48 hours if cultures negative + well.
cards.context:
EONS (<72 h) is dominated by vertically transmitted maternal flora — GBS and E. coli account for ~70%.

Empirical antibiotics target both: benzylpenicillin (GBS, Listeria, syphilis) + gentamicin (E. coli and other Gram-negatives, synergistic with penicillin against GBS); doses benzylpen 60 mg/kg IV 12-hourly.

LONS (>72 h) more often nosocomial — flucloxacillin (Staph) + gent. Add aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 8-hourly if HSV suspected (vesicles, focal neurology, maternal active genital herpes).

cards.front: Tranexamic acid should be given within [___] of birth for PPH at a dose of 1 g IV (WOMAN trial evidence).
cards.context:
The WOMAN trial (2017) demonstrated that IV tranexamic acid 1g given within 3 hours of birth reduces death from bleeding in women with PPH, with no increase in thromboembolic events.

It should be given early — benefit decreases with each hour of delay. WHO recommends TXA within 3 hours for all women with PPH.

cards.front: Initial intrauterine resuscitation for prolonged fetal bradycardia: maternal repositioning and stop [___]; if persistent, proceed to category 1 caesarean.
cards.context:
Prolonged fetal bradycardia (FHR <110 for >3 min) is a peripartum emergency. If unresolved by 9 min or with an abnormal CTG, proceed to category 1 caesarean.

Caesarean urgency (RANZCOG): Cat 1 = immediate threat to mother/fetus, deliver ≤30 min; Cat 2 = compromise without immediate threat, ≤75 min; Cat 3 = early delivery, no compromise; Cat 4 = elective.

cards.front: Elevated middle cerebral artery (MCA) peak systolic velocity (>1.5 multiples of the median) suggests fetal anaemia; treatment may require intrauterine [___].
cards.context:
Fetal anaemia drops blood viscosity, which paradoxically RAISES peak systolic velocity in the MCA — the brain compensates for reduced O₂ carriage by increasing flow.

When PSV crosses threshold, refer urgently to MFM for IUT via cordocentesis.

cards.front: Recurrent miscarriage is now defined as 2 or more pregnancy losses <20 weeks (down from the previous [___]+ threshold).
cards.context:
Recurrent miscarriage is defined as two or more confirmed intrauterine pregnancy losses before 20 weeks. Important actionable causes include antiphospholipid syndrome and uterine anomalies.

Test for anticardiolipin, lupus anticoagulant and anti-β2GP1; positivity must persist at least 12 weeks apart to confirm APS.

Analyse pregnancy tissue when available. Consider parental karyotyping case by case, including when tissue analysis is unavailable.

cards.front: After the fetal head delivers, it untwists slightly to realign with the shoulders — this movement is called [___].
cards.context:
Restitution is the small reverse rotation of the delivered head, realigning it with the shoulders' position in the pelvis.

It precedes the larger external rotation that accompanies shoulder engagement with the AP diameter.

cards.front: The first mechanical step in managing postpartum haemorrhage from atony is uterine [___].
cards.context: Most PPH is uterine atony, so the first mechanical step is to rub up a contraction — bimanual uterine massage — alongside uterotonics (oxytocin first). Escalate to surgical measures only if bleeding continues.
